sentences.text:
The Hon'Ble Sri Justice K.Surender
 Criminal Revision Case No.1594 of 2009
Order:

This Criminal Revision Case is filed against the Judgment dated 31.08.2009 in Criminal Appeal No.36 of 2009 on the file of the II Additional Sessions Judge, Karimnagar at Jagtial, whereunder the sentence of conviction imposed against the petitioner/accused No.1 in C.C.No.546 of 2008 on the file of the Judicial First Class Magistrate, Jagtial, was confirmed for the offences under Section 498A of IPC and Section 4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961.
2.

entities.text: II Additional Sessions Judge, Karimnagar at Jagtial
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Heard learned counsel for the petitioner as well as learned Additional Public Prosecutor appearing for the respondent-State and perused the record.
3. The revision petitioner is the husband, who was convicted by the both the Courts below for the said offences as indicated above.
The parents of the petitioner were also prosecuted by the trial Court, however, they were acquitted by the trial Court.
4. Briefly, the case of the prosecution is that the marriage of the de facto complainant-PW.1 and the petitioner was performed on 03.10.1994.
They were blessed with two sons.
They led normal matrimonial life for three years.
When PW.1 questioned the illegal activities of the petitioner, he started harassing her both physically and mentally.
There was demand of additional dowry of Rs.20,000/- for which reason a panchayat was held.
With the intervention of the elders, PW.1 joined the petitioner.
Further, the accused did not change their attitude and again started harassing PW.1 for an amount of Rs.80,000/- for which reason she was beaten up on 01.07.2003.
Aggrieved by the said conduct, a complaint was filed with the police.
5. Police have investigated into the same and filed charge sheet for the offences under Section 498A of IPC and Section 4 of the D.P. Act.

6. Learned Magistrate having examined PWs.1 to 6 and also based on Exs.P.1 to P.4, which were brought on record by the prosecution, found favour with the version of PW.1 and convicted the petitioner and acquitted accused Nos.2 and 3.
7.
The said conviction was questioned in the Appeal before the Sessions Court.
The learned Sessions Judge dismissed the Appeal and confirmed the conviction.
8. In the course of trial, defence was taken that false complaint was filed and there was any amount of contradictory evidence regarding the demand of dowry.
Initially the witnesses stated that Rs.50,000/- was demanded, however, the evidence is that Rs.80,000/- was demanded.

sentences.text: Even in the course of investigation, the said woman was not identified.
9. Having gone through the record, it is obvious that the main grievance of PW.1 was suspicion that this petitioner was having relation with another woman.
However, the investigation did not reveal that the petitioner had any kind of illicit relation with any other woman.
10. The other allegation regarding demand for dowry is vague and the evidence of witnesses is contradictory regarding the quantum of dowry.
However, keeping in view that the marriage of the petitioner and PW.1 had taken place in the year 1994, complaint was filed in the year 2003 and 21 years have passed by

, this Court in the present circumstances is inclined to reduce the sentence of imprisonment to the period already undergone by the revision petitioner, which upholding the conviction under both counts.
11. Accordingly, this Criminal Revision Case is allowed in- part.
Pending miscellaneous petitions, if any, shall stand closed.
K.SURENDER, J Date : 15.07.2024 ynk Nagasamudrala Ganga Chari vs The State Of A.P. on 15 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/125382515/
